b2-129.title: Sports news
b2-129.story: Max was writing the sports page for the school newspaper, and Anna offered to help. First came athletics: a local [[sprinter]] had broken the city record in the 100 meters. Then came football, where a striker from their school scored a [[hat trick]] thanks to some brilliant [[dribbling]]. The school [[futsal]] team had also won, and Sofia's [[water polo]] team finished second at the regional tournament. Anna added a short piece about the new [[squash]] courts near the metro. Max wanted to include betting odds from a [[bookmaker]], but Anna reminded him that most of their readers were under eighteen. Instead, they wrote about a racing driver whose slow [[pit stop]] had cost him the win, and about a boy from their street who came third in a [[motocross]] race. On Monday, the coach read the whole page aloud in the schoolyard through a [[megaphone]], and Max couldn't stop smiling.

b2-130.title: Martial arts class
b2-130.story: Lisa had been doing [[kickboxing]] for a year, and she finally convinced Anna to try a class at her gym. The coach, a former professional [[kickboxer]], started with a warm-up that left Anna completely out of breath. In the next room, a group was practicing [[aikido]], using their partners' energy instead of force. Lisa explained that she had also tried [[jiu-jitsu]], but she preferred fighting on her feet rather than on the floor. On the wall hung an old [[katana]], which the coach said had belonged to his own teacher. After class, Max turned up at the café downstairs and challenged both girls to [[arm wrestling]]. Lisa beat him in seconds, and Anna nearly did too. Max laughed and decided that maybe he should sign up for the beginner class as well.

b2-131.title: Winter games
b2-131.story: Anna's family spent the winter holidays at a small ski resort in the mountains. Every evening, Grandpa watched the winter games on TV and cheered for every athlete. On the first night, a Ukrainian skier came third in the [[slalom]], and Grandpa nearly jumped off the sofa. The next day, Taras insisted that the family ride down the hill on one long sled like a [[bobsleigh]] team, with Dad steering at the front. Mama preferred watching the [[biathlon]], although she admitted she would be terrible at both skiing and shooting. Meanwhile, a young [[snowboarder]] showed Anna how to come down the slope in a slow [[zigzag]] instead of going straight. By the afternoon, Taras and Grandma had built a small [[igloo]] behind the hotel. Grandpa crawled inside for a photo and declared it the best event of the whole winter.

b2-132.title: An extreme weekend
b2-132.story: For Max's birthday, Lisa and Ira planned an extreme weekend at an adventure park outside the city. Max had always said he wanted to try [[bungee jumping]], but when he saw the platform, he suddenly went quiet. So they started with the [[zipline]] instead, flying high above the trees while Sofia screamed with joy. Later, they watched a [[parachutist]] float slowly down and land right next to the parking lot. In the afternoon, they went [[kayaking]] on the lake, and Ira fell into the water twice. Their instructor turned out to run a local [[diving club]], and she invited them to a free trial lesson at the [[dive center]] next month. On Sunday, a professional [[stuntman]] gave a show, jumping a motorcycle over three cars. After that, some local teens showed off their [[parkour]] moves, and a [[skateboarder]] did a flip right in front of Max. On the way home, Max said it was his best birthday ever and promised to be braver next year.

b2-133.title: The dog show
b2-133.story: On Saturday, Anna and Max volunteered at the city dog show in the park. Their first job was to hold a sleepy [[bulldog]] that refused to walk into the ring. Next to them, a woman was brushing her white [[poodle]] until its fur looked like a cloud. A tiny [[terrier]] barked at everyone who walked past, including the judges. Meanwhile, a [[beagle]] escaped from its owner and followed the smell of sausages to the food tent. Max was nervous around a big [[pit bull]], but it turned out to be the friendliest dog at the show. Anna fell in love with a [[husky]] whose eyes were as blue as the sky. In the end, first prize went to a clever [[collie]] that did every trick perfectly. On the way home, Anna asked her mama for the hundredth time if they could get a dog.

b2-134.title: Storm warning
b2-134.story: One evening, a storm warning appeared on Anna's phone, so she and Ira stayed in and worked on their geography project about extreme weather. Ira explained how an earthquake under the ocean can cause a [[tsunami]] that reaches the coast within minutes. Anna found out that a [[typhoon]] and a [[cyclone]] are basically the same kind of storm, just with different names in different parts of the world. When the rain finally stopped, Dad looked out the window and said that at least the storm had cleared the [[smog]] over the city. That gave the girls an idea for a section on pollution and the [[ozone]] layer, which protects us from the sun's harmful rays. At the end, they added tips for an [[eco]] lifestyle, such as taking the metro and recycling plastic. On Friday, the teacher gave them the top grade, and Ira joked that their presentation had taken the class by storm.

b2-135.title: A day at the zoo
b2-135.story: Anna took Taras to the zoo for his birthday, and he made a list of every animal he wanted to see. First they found a [[leopard]] sleeping lazily on a branch, its tail hanging down. At the reptile house, Taras pressed his nose against the glass to look at an [[alligator]], which didn't move at all. A [[chameleon]] slowly turned from green to brown, while a huge [[python]] lay curled up under a heat lamp. Their favorite was a young [[orangutan]] who kept stealing his mother's banana. Next door, a [[lemur]] with a long striped tail jumped from rope to rope. In the insect house, a guide showed them a [[termite]] nest taller than Taras and a butterfly slowly breaking out of its [[cocoon]]. On the way out, they passed a bed of bright roses, and a sign explained that each one was a [[hybrid]] of two wild species. Taras checked off the last item on his list and announced that he wanted to be a zookeeper.

b2-136.title: With the park ranger
b2-136.story: During a summer exchange program in the American West, Anna and Max joined a guided hike in a national park. Their guide, a friendly [[ranger]] named Joe, promised them an amazing view from the [[peak]] before lunch. On the way up, he pointed at the deep red [[canyon]] below and explained that the river had been cutting it for millions of years. The trail passed huge gray rocks of [[granite]] and an old [[cedar]] that was older than the country itself. Near the top, Joe showed them black stones that had once been hot [[lava]]. He said they might hear a [[coyote]] at night, and that a herd of [[bison]] sometimes blocked the road near the entrance. Max nervously asked about dangerous animals, and Joe admitted that a [[puma]] had been seen nearby last spring. From the top, the park looked endless, and Joe said it covered more than a hundred thousand [[hectares|hectare]]. Max took dozens of photos, but he kept glancing at the bushes the whole way down.
